washer-repair.repairTips: If your Plainfield home has a second-floor laundry room, invest in a drain pan under the washer and a water leak sensor — these inexpensive safeguards can prevent thousands of dollars in ceiling and floor damage. Replace rubber supply hoses with braided stainless steel lines; the rubber hoses installed at build time in many Plainfield homes are often past their recommended 5-year lifespan. For front-load washers, wipe down the door gasket after every use and leave the door cracked to prevent the mold buildup that thrives in Plainfield's humid summers.

refrigerator-and-freezer-repair.localInsights: Many Plainfield homes feature open-concept kitchen layouts where the refrigerator is positioned near large windows or adjacent to cooking areas. refrigerator-and-freezer-repair.repairTips: Keep your refrigerator's condenser coils clean — in Plainfield homes with pets, dust and hair accumulate on these coils within a few months and significantly reduce cooling efficiency. Set the refrigerator temperature to 37°F and the freezer to 0°F; every degree colder than necessary increases energy use by about 5% and strains the compressor during Plainfield's hot summer months.
